# ADR-049 — A sleep session is attributed to, and queried on, its civil END (wake) date

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**A sleep session is attributed to, and queried on, its civil END (wake) date.** `attributed_local_date = civilEndTime.date`; exercise is attributed to its civil **start** date. Three reasons, the second decisive: it matches the mental model ("how did I sleep last night?" is asked the morning after); the `daily-*` types computed from the sleep period (`daily-resting-heart-rate`, `daily-heart-rate-variability`, `daily-sleep-temperature-derivations`) are reported by Google on one civil date, so wake-date attribution is what keeps a `sleep`-to-`daily-hrv` join from being off by one; and it is total, since every session has a civil end date. **The API makes this free rather than merely convenient**: `list` documents `sleep.interval.end_time` / `sleep.interval.civil_end_time` as sleep-exclusive filters and explicitly excludes sleep from the generic session-start filter, so the attribution rule, the fetch filter and the deletion-reconciliation scope are **one and the same axis** — no start-time query with a compensating one-day widening is needed or correct. The rule lives in exactly one function (`packages/core/src/health/day-attribution.ts`) and **every input is stored**, so changing it is a local `UPDATE` plus re-derivation with no re-fetch and no migration (Phase 6 Checkpoint 6.0, user-approved 2026-08-24)
